section_summary: This section contains State Department records from January and July 1933 regarding disarmament efforts and easing tensions in American-Japanese relations. It includes reports on Professor James T. Shotwell's address at the Conference on the Cause and Cure of War concerning disarmament, arbitration, and moral disarmament, alongside press reports of upcoming Japanese naval maneuvers in mandated Pacific islands. In response to potential friction from concurrent American fleet operations off Hawaii, Far Eastern Affairs official Maxwell M. Hamilton proposes extending a goodwill invitation to the Japanese fleet to make a courtesy call at Manila or Honolulu, an initiative later noted by Stanley K. Hornbeck as having been partially achieved by subsequent naval visits.

subfiles.about: Report and press account of Professor James T. Shotwell's address before the Conference on the Cause and Cure of War on disarmament and moral disarmament.
keywords: Conference on the Cause and Cure of War
subfiles.summary: Shotwell urges disarmament through League/World Court cooperation eliminating arms' root causes; Woolley and McDonald praise the Stimson Doctrine on Manchuria; Shotwell endorses Poland's moral-disarmament proposal via education and anti-propaganda measures.
subfiles.title: Riddance to Need of Arms Is Urged: Address by Professor James T. Shotwell on Disarmament and Moral Disarmament

subfiles.about: A note observing that reciprocal naval visits have substantially achieved the objectives of an earlier memorandum on improving American-Japanese relations.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says the Japanese training squadron's and Admiral Taylor's visits largely met earlier goodwill goals, recommending the memo be filed or forwarded to Communications and Records.
subfiles.title: Visit of Japanese Training Squadron and Admiral Taylor's Visit

subfiles.about: A memorandum proposing a goodwill invitation to the Japanese fleet to visit Manila or Honolulu to ease naval tensions in the Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton, prompted by reports of Japanese naval maneuvers near mandated islands, proposes inviting Japan's fleet to Manila or Honolulu to ease U.S.-fleet tensions, outlining informal soundings via the naval attaché, Grew, and the Navy Department.
subfiles.title: American-Japanese Relations: Possible Means of Improving

subfiles.about: A Washington Post clipping reporting on scheduled Japanese naval maneuvers in the mandated Pacific islands and American naval maneuvers off Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: AP report: Navy Minister Osumi denies hostile intent for early southward maneuvers near mandated islands; Honolulu's Taketomi acknowledges concern over U.S. fleet concentration as American ships gather for Pacific war games.
subfiles.title: Entire Tokyo Navy To Maneuver Near American Islands
